en: In the *Cirenwen bashizhonghao jing* (Sūtra on Maitreya Asking about the Eighty Minor Marks), Maitreya asks the Buddha: "By what causes and conditions are the eighty minor marks manifested? The Buddha replied:

"First, because in life after life one has directed thoughts of equanimity toward others, one obtains the mark of level soles that leave an impression upon the ground. Second, [because one has] honored people..."
Because he gives whatever others take pleasure in so that they may be at ease;
thus, he attains a well-proportioned, beautiful, and clearly defined physical form.
Third, because he is harmonious with others, people who see him always rejoice.
Your elegant words cause those who receive this scripture to be enlightened without exception.
Fourthly, because mounds and walls are uneven and produce thorns, they must be cleared away;
thus, your conduct is moistened and radiant, and your practice is ever secure.
Fifth, because he has never harbored resentment toward others nor incited strife among them,
his calves are fine, soft, and well-proportioned, and his stride is infinite. Sixth,
because whenever he saw deep pits, mud, or water, he immediately constructed bridges over them.
The ground he treads upon is peaceful and auspicious.
Seventh, he displays tens of millions of kinds of objects arranged along the path as an act of giving.
When the wheels and spokes beneath his feet form rows, he preaches the sutras.
Eighth, because wherever he is, he invariably increases the lifespan of the people of the world;
thus, with the spokes of his wheel corresponding [to his virtues], he naturally attains the status of Great Honored One.
Ninth, because wherever he is, he bestows profound sutras, both teaching them himself and instructing others to do so.
The soles of his feet are entirely deep.
Tenth, wherever he is gentle and benevolent, he regards all people with such [compassion] that the dust does not settle upon the soles of his feet, which are soft and supple.
Eleventh, because one does not enumerate the faults of others nor cause them to harbor resentment;
thus, you should direct your mind toward the ten directions with complete sincerity and a virtuous intention.
Twelfth, because wherever you are, you teach people in due order without indolence.
The joints of his toes are perfectly straight.
Thirteenth, because he has recited the merits of the Buddha,
the soles of his feet are beautifully marked with auspicious signs.
Fourteenth, because he plants trees, provides wells, and constructs bathing pools along the roadsides, he is named "Renowned.
Fifteenth, because he resolves the doubts and difficulties of others without any sense of attachment or stinginess.
16. His nails are the color of red copper.
Because he has always brought his tasks to completion and is loved and honored by others such that they never part from him, his toes are marked with auspicious signs;
born into a noble lineage, he attains Buddhahood, and there is no one capable of surpassing him.
Seventeenth, because his observance of the precepts is unshakable,
he knows all that is done by those who are arrogant, even down to their toes.
Eighteenth, because his observance of the precepts does not involve a wish to be reborn in the heavens.
The toes are even.
Nineteenth, because those of noble lineage do not easily engage in evil,
they are naked, level, and fall [in step], knowing the intentions of others.
Twentieth, because one does not covet the questions asked but explains them accordingly,
one attains unsurpassed wisdom.
Twenty-first, because one maintains diligence for oneself.
His body is naked, moist, and radiant; he knows all the evil intentions of people.
Twenty-second: because of his utmost sincerity, though his body is naked, it is not fettered, and he knows what is being thought in the minds of others.
Twenty-third: [He] desires that all who hear the sutras may know them before others; that all who hear the Buddha preach the sutras shall delight in questioning him;
and that he shall obtain physical strength such that none can break or crush it.
Twenty-fourth, because he bestows the sūtras upon others,
his body is fully endowed with the ability to preach the truths of the sūtras without error.
Twenty-fifth, because when others preach the sūtras they can never be stopped, and he bestows the sūtras upon others in their entirety.
His body was broad, expansive, and perfectly formed; when he preached the sutras, all classes of beings, including insects and crawling creatures, heard and understood him.
Twenty-sixth, because those with doubts were resolved by means of the Buddha’s Tripitaka.
Excellence, rectitude, nobility, and goodness.
Twenty-seventh: he does not wound the bodies or minds of others, nor does he mock them with facial expressions.
For this reason, he attains the eighty minor marks, such that all who see him are without fail filled with joy.
Twenty-eighth: seeing women who are ill, he treats them with a mind of wisdom;
for this reason, his body is upright, noble, and peerless.
Twenty-ninth: by bathing and washing the human body, he purifies it and removes the three impurities.
His body is pure and clean, its radiance illuminating the ten directions.
Thirtieth: because he immediately respects those who are arrogant and disrespectful and disciplines them through tranquility, his body is supple and lustrous.
Thirty-first, because he does not act as a matchmaker nor engage in scheming for others,
his countenance is free from distress, and he need have no fear. Thirty-second,
because he gives medicine to those who are ill to restore them to health, he has no cause for sorrow or anxiety.
Thirty-third: Because he does not display a smile when seeing those who are not upright or virtuous, but instead completes their excellence, his Buddha-body is lustrous, moist, and pure.
Thirty-fourth: Because he encourages and delights others in performing meritorious deeds and practicing goodness.
He delivers those whose bodies are situated in evil realms.

Thirty-fifth: because he inquires after and massages those he sees who are exhausted, hungry, and thirsty, his back becomes level and beautiful, and it also heals others of the disease of sensual desire.
Thirty-sixth: Because he rejoices greatly upon seeing others perform wholesome deeds, the two collarbones are level from top to bottom, and he fully knows the minds of others.
Thirty-seventh: Because he bestows the precepts according to what people delight in, and causes them to practice patience and restrain their thoughts.
In both villages, they were fond of performing sutra recitations according to the proper sequence.
As for the thirty-eighth [practice]: seeing a woman in labor, one assists her with a mind of compassion so that she may give birth smoothly and quickly.
Thirty-ninth: He is deeply devoted to the liberation of others and possesses the root of loving-kindness and compassion;
he does not harbor anger or resentment, his actions are never erroneous, and he instructs those who lack reverence.
The *cīvara* is rounded and elevated.
Those who are forty years old teach themselves and others by means of the precepts received from their teachers;
thus, they practice giving in accordance with the principles of discipline.
Forty-first: Because he himself does not engage in lust and likewise restrains the minds of others, when descending from his mount among the Hu, he purges his belly so that no impurities remain.
Forty-second: Because he delights in the joy of human beings and does not disrupt their peace and stability, nor involve them in the affairs of ordinary men.
The marks of his body are perfected such that they cannot be destroyed, like celestial tempered iron;
forty-third, because he dwells with a mind of loving-kindness toward all people in the world with equanimity,
both his shoulders are full and rounded.
Forty-fourth: because his thoughts are vast and expansive, teaching others to do good until they are fully perfected;
therefore, his two shoulders are broad and great, and his knowledge is profoundly deep.
Forty-fifth: because his wisdom is courageous and robust, and he maintains his mind without wavering.
His two arms are hollow and long, and on his fingertips there are the characters for "ten thousand.
Forty-sixth: because he does not speak of deceitful arrogance or matters of sexual misconduct;
his lips and mouth are like vermilion, free from odors or impurities.
Forty-seventh: He does not suppress the consciousness of others, for he is free from anger and deceitful attitudes;
his speech is neither too loud nor too low, but perfectly moderate, as if holding a morsel in his mouth.
Forty-eighth: Because he gave the flavors of the five fragrances and the five medicinal herbs to others, his tongue is free from impurity.
Forty-ninth: Because he does not mock others with facial expressions nor revile others.
There are none among those who hear his words who do not rejoice and attain liberation.
At fifty, he upholds the precepts and practices contemplation, refraining from speaking of women;
with his sharp, rounded, and firm teeth, he uses the power of his insight to destroy craving and desire.
Fifty-first: By discerning the essentials, he resolves the doubts and difficulties of others;
his tusks are firm and sharp, shattering and dispersing craving and desire.
Fifty-second: When asked about a single matter, he explains it in order to resolve numerous issues.
The fifty-third [type of person] is one who follows the heterodox paths (tīrthika) in succession;
because they mix various fragrant oils and apply them into their nostrils,
they possess an extraordinary refinement such that they never perceive a foul odor, but only smell fragrance.
Fifty-fourth: Because he saw heaps of excrement being swept away and discarded, his radiance is pure and clean, and he looks upon people with kind eyes.
Fifty-fifth: Because he has honored the Buddha-images in every lifetime.
His eyes were long and excellent; there was no scripture he did not understand.
Fifty-sixth: because in life after life he gazed upon others with a pure mind, his eyes were like those of a *karkoṭaka* snake, such that nothing he looked at failed to be seen.
Fifty-seventh: Because throughout successive lifetimes he saw people’s wealth and nobility yet his mind felt no greed or delight, his eyes were neither too large nor too small;
they were clearly focused upon the middle way, never gazing about aimlessly.
Fifty-eighth: Because of his benevolent mind and peaceful heart throughout successive lifetimes, his vision is unclouded as he gazes upon the heavens above and the world below.
Fifty-ninth: Because he was unable to recognize [them] throughout successive lifetimes.
His eyes were clear and bright; he did not smile at others nor did he stare at them, for he did not gaze upon women.
His eyebrows and eyes were so clear and beautiful that among those with whom he interacted, he was a master.
At sixty, he constantly reflected upon his past lives and likewise contemplated the goodness of others.
His eyebrows are as beautiful as a half-moon, perceiving all matters throughout the ten directions.
Sixty-first: because he has never harbored anger or changed countenance from lifetime to lifetime, his eyebrows are lustrous.
Sixty-second: because his mind has been perfectly equanimous toward enemies and kinsmen from lifetime to lifetime, his eyebrows are supple and moist.
Sixty-third: Because in life after life he delighted in serving wise teachers and desired to understand the subtle and profound sutras of the future, his eyebrows are a deep blue-black color.
Sixty-fourth: Because in life after life, when seeing others preaching the sutras, he did not seek out their faults to report to others.
Sixty-fifth: His ears hear the sounds of the heavens.
From lifetime to lifetime, he does not have ears like those of a householder; his ears do not rest upon his head, nor are they attached to his hands or feet.
His ears are neither too large nor too small, but are perfectly proportioned, moist, beautiful, and do not perceive [unwholesome] sounds.
Sixty-sixth: because those who see him in life after life and practice the path with self-restraint do not dare to alarm or frighten him, he does not forget the matters he has recognized.
Sixty-seventh: because the meaning of the sutras and dharmas he hears in life after life neither increases nor decreases, [he retains them].
The forehead is six inches long, from which majestic spiritual power arises.
Sixty-eighth: because he has taught and guided throughout successive lifetimes in proper sequence, his hair is glossy and well-ordered according to its growth, remaining free from dust and grime.

Sixty-ninth: Because in life after life he has always spoken to others with a harmonious countenance and a pleasant expression, never using abusive language or harsh speech, his hair is fine and beautiful beyond compare.

Seventieth: Because in life after life he has venerated teachers and wise people who uphold the precepts, and because he has given offerings of clarified butter, sesame oil, and the garments he himself wore to others, [his hair is fragrant].
Seventy-first: Because he has instructed people through various meritorious deeds in every lifetime, his hair is glossy and beautiful;
it is even and uniform without gaps or deficiencies, such that there is no one who beholds his hair and does not rejoice.
Seventy-second: Because from lifetime to lifetime one perceives the right and wrong of others but does not transmit their good or evil deeds, defilements and dust do not adhere to them;
even when entering [the world], they do not perceive the evil of others.
Seventy-third: Because he has never extinguished the lamps before the Buddhas or the lamps of humans throughout successive lifetimes, dust and grime do not adhere to his hair, which remains radiant.
Seventy-fourth: Because throughout successive lifetimes he has given others crowns, tiaras, *maochan* (fox-fur hats), hair-covers, turbans, mats, and cushions with a benevolent mind.
The hair-whorls grow in clusters with majestic spiritual power, such that one never tires of beholding them.
The seventy-fifth is the mark of spreading his hair so that his parents and teachers may tread upon it;
by this mark of the hair-whorls, he perceives the thoughts of those in the ten directions.
Seventy-sixth: Because in life after life he always gave generously to those who desired precious objects, his hair is everywhere even and uniform, and he fulfills all his wishes. Seventy-seventh:

Because in life after life he wished that others would follow the precepts rather than seeking material gain from him, and he constantly aspired to associate with virtuous teachers and those who clarify the scriptures, he performs his duties in accordance with them.
The patterns of his hair arise between them like a vase; through his majestic karma, his voice reaches the ten directions.
Seventy-eighth: because he has taught his fellow students and those who study the scriptures throughout successive lives, his hair is even and his mind is concentrated.
Seventy-ninth: Because in every lifetime he has completed whatever he undertook to learn, his merit is perfected.
Eightieth: Because in every lifetime he constantly benefits others, bringing them peace and security.
The teachings spoken with a compassionate mind are vast, profound, moistening, and sublime, without end or limit.
Such has been the conduct of the Bodhisattva throughout successive lifetimes.
[This concludes] the *Compassionate Inquiry on the Sūtra of the Eighty Minor Marks*.
